reason: E3 shows that thermal management (insulation, ~500°C preheat) reduces cracking in a different alloy and process (L-DED of CrNbTiZr), but provides no direct evidence for LPBF of CoCrFeMnNi or for the claimed improvements in dimensional precision and mechanical properties. E1 and E2 only describe general defect formation mechanisms and parameter ranges, offering no specific support for the 550°C preheating intervention or its predicted outcomes.
premises: Preheating to ~550°C reduces thermal gradients and residual stresses in LPBF CoCrFeMnNi
Reduced thermal gradients suppress cracking and improve interlayer fusion
Enhanced inert atmosphere controls can mitigate oxidation at 550°C
Reduced defects improve dimensional precision and mechanical integrity
The mechanism observed in L-DED of CrNbTiZr (E3) generalizes to LPBF of CoCrFeMnNi
